author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do people trust referrals more than even the most sophisticated sales outreach? In this thought-provoking talk, Stephen Oommen explores the growing trust gap in business and argues that real growth comes not from scaling activity, but from becoming genuinely “referable.” Drawing on decades of leadership experience in enterprise sales, he challenges audiences to rethink networking, reputation, and human connection in an increasingly automated world — and makes the case that relationships remain the most valuable currency we have. 

Stephen Oommen is a go-to-market leader, keynote speaker, and sales strategist with leadership experience at Microsoft, Outreach, and Accenture. Over his career, he has helped scale global teams and drive nine-figure revenue growth while championing a more human approach to business development. Through his “Go-to-Network” philosophy, Stephen focuses on the power of trust, relationships, and reputation in modern sales and leadership.

title: How to build a reputation that gets you job referrals | Stephen Oommen | TEDxUNYP

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Our anxiety about a world with artificial intelligence may be misdirected — Historically, the real trust crisis, is not in the machine, but in the humans feeding it. Drawing on over twenty years advising leaders and CEOs, Shani Lehrer names AI as our most honest mirror, amplifying whatever we bring to it — fear or courage, ego or sovereignty. In this talk, she offers a method for staying true to who we are, so we can be trustworthy stewards for AI to emulate and amplify, not the worst, but the best of our magnificent humanity. Shani Lehrer is a strategic consultant, founder and creator of the Inner Geopolitics Method — a framework for inner leadership and how to navigate internal states with the same clarity and precision typically applied to external systems and global challenges.

Over the past two decades, she has worked with world leaders, Fortune 500 executives, elite athletes, and artists, bridging advanced mind management with authentic, impactful leadership.

title: AI doesn't have a trust problem. We do! | Shani Lehrer | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk centers on a simple but powerful insight: the gift you give best is often the one you needed most. Drawing from psychology, leadership, and personal experience, he explores how many of our greatest strengths began as solutions to something we once lacked. Over time we become highly skilled at giving that gift to others yet rarely learn how to receive it ourselves. But when we finally do, the gift that we once gave automatically becomes something we can offer intentionally, changing the way we lead, relate, and show up in the moments that matter. Jason VanRuler became fascinated by a quiet pattern he kept seeing in his work: some of the most generous, successful and dependable people were also the most exhausted. Growing up in the Midwest, he was the kid who felt deeply, asked questions about relationships, and, as he jokes, “always dressed like a therapist.” After early success in the recruiting industry, that curiosity eventually led him into psychology, where he began work
title: The Gift You Give Best Is the One You Needed Most | Jason VanRuler | TEDxSioux Falls

author: TEDx Talks
description: In 1993, Vince Danh's parents moved to Sioux Falls and opened the first Vietnamese restaurant in town. They spent their lives in the Back of House — the kitchen — trading 14-hour days for their family's future. Vince stepped through the swinging door into the Front of House. He has the degrees, the safety, and the meaningful work they sacrificed for. And yet, success feels like a betrayal. Drawing on research and his own lived experience, Vince explores the "Immigrant Paradox" — why second-generation immigrants, who should be thriving, often struggle more than their parents did. The guilt runs deep. But this talk offers a reframe: culture, community, and belonging are not luxuries the Bridge Generation stumbled into. They are exactly what their parents' labor was meant to purchase. This talk is a call to stop apologizing for stepping through the door — and to start honoring the sacrifice by holding it open for everyone else. Vince Danh grew up behind the counter of his family's restau
title: The Swinging Door: From Survival to Significance | Vince Danh | TEDxSioux Falls

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a South Bronx classroom, Sarah learned how loving the children in her classes unconditionally transformed the way the classroom community functioned and allowed students to reach for excellence. The key was love. For the Ancient Greeks, the highest form of love is agape - a verb - which means the deliberate choice to will the good of others. This talk explores how love expression can further our relationships, workplace, and larger community with impacts that can be measured in outcomes rather than intention. Sarah grew up in Sioux Falls, SD in a loving family. An avid learner, Sarah traveled extensively during and after college, and began her career teaching in the South Bronx before transitioning into non-profit leadership. After nearly a decade in New York, Sarah and her husband Shane, and their two children, returned to Sioux Falls in 2021. Sarah is passionate about building strong communities through human connection and making deliberate choices to will the good of others. Th
title: More than a feeling | Sarah Meagher | TEDxSioux Falls

author: TEDx Talks
description: Emily pulls back the curtain on how communication works on a television set, from one-way directives to collaborative meaning-making, and how one actor’s simple decision to shake hands with the “extras” transformed the entire energy of a production. Drawing on symbolic interactionism and servant leadership theory, she reveals a powerful truth: people don’t rise because of status. They rise because someone chose to see them.  This is a talk for anyone who has ever felt blurry in someone else’s story and for anyone who has the power to bring someone else into focus. Being essential isn’t about how many scenes you’re in. It’s about how fully you show up for the ones you have. Emily Magera is a communication specialist, choreographer, and fine arts educator based in South Dakota. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Communication Studies and Theatre from the University of Sioux Falls and Master’s degree in Communication and Leadership Studies from Gonzaga University.  Before returning to Sout
title: From Extra to Essential | Emily Magera | TEDxSioux Falls

author: TEDx Talks
description: We've built a culture that treats leaders like products — rated, blamed, and discarded when they disappoint. But what does that cost the person inside the role? Drawing on a decade of confidential conversations with leaders across industries, Customer Culture exposes the hidden psychological toll of a world that demands everything from its leaders and gives almost nothing back — and issues an urgent call to replace a culture of consumption with one of community, before the wrong people are the only ones still willing to lead. Vaney Hariri is a Sioux Falls-based strategist, facilitator, and keynote speaker, and co-founder of Think 3D Solutions. For over a decade, Vaney has worked at the intersection of leadership development and civic engagement — building programs like Leaders of Tomorrow and the Bridging the Gap initiative, and developing frameworks that help organizations and communities grow with intention. A 2019 TEDxSiouxFalls speaker ("Low on Leaders"), Vaney is known for direct
title: The problem with leadership culture today | Vaney Hariri | TEDxSioux Falls

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a culture defined by "high-definition exhaustion," we often prioritize the speed of a transaction over the depth of a connection. Drawing on her Ethiopian heritage, Afomiya Dejene explores the "slow brew"—a cultural framework of intentionality—as a vital tool for navigating modern human interaction. Dejene argues that the most effective way to dismantle bias and bridge societal divides is through the restorative power of genuine presence. By moving beyond surface-level exchanges and embracing the patience required for real dialogue, we can transform potentially divisive moments into opportunities for mutual understanding. This talk is a call to reclaim conversation not just as a means of communication, but as a deliberate act of seeing and being seen. Afomiya Dejene was born in Ethiopia, Africa, and immigrated to the United States at the age of four with her parents and older sister. After graduating from Roosevelt High School in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, Afomiya is now a student
title: The power of conversation | Afomiya Dejene | TEDxSioux Falls

author: TEDx Talks
description: Past relational experiences aren't failures; they show us where healing and deeper self-love are needed. We don't find love - we reflect it, because every relationship in our life is a mirror of how deeply we've learned to love ourselves. Host of the Spotify Top 50 podcast Project Loving Myself, Sanaiyah Gurnamal is a transformational speaker, certified coach, and visionary leader. Known as the “Love Alchemist,” she helps high-achievers make love their power move—in life, relationships, and business. Sanaiyah is the relationship expert for Cosmopolitan magazine, has been featured on CNN four times, and is the founder of The Third Eye Wellness, a premier wellbeing center. Her philosophy—that self-love is your greatest source of power—inspires women to become their top priority, biggest fan, and loudest cheerleader. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Mirror Effect Of Love: Every Relationship Reflects | Sanaiyah Gurnamal | TEDxChinotimba

description:
You know what you need to do. So why is it still so hard to do it?

Most of us assume that once we become aware of our habits, fears, and limiting beliefs, change will naturally follow. 

But what if awareness is only the beginning?

In this TEDx talk, entrepreneur and speaker Ameka Coleman explores why insight alone often falls short of creating lasting transformation. Drawing from her own journey through personal growth and entrepreneurship, she challenges the idea that knowing ourselves is enough to move us forward.

Instead, Ameka introduces a different perspective: meaningful change requires more than self-awareness, it requires self-leadership. 

By learning to lead ourselves through fear, uncertainty, and discomfort, we become better equipped to take the actions that shape who we become.

Whether you’re pursuing a personal goal, navigating a life transition, or striving to become the person you know you’re capable of being, this talk offers a powerful invitation to move beyond
title: Self-awareness alone won’t change your life  | Ameka Coleman | TEDxGreenwood

description: Sustainability is not defined by occasional actions but by the habits we build every day. Drawing on his experience in engineering, procurement, logistics, and facilities management, Akwondytiem (AJ) Otu explores how small, consistent changes in individual and organisational behaviour can drive meaningful environmental impact. From the workplace to daily life, he demonstrates how embedding sustainable habits into our routines can create lasting change and help shape a more resilient future. AJ has a bachelor’s in mechanical engineering & masters in Procurement, Logistics & Supply Chain Management. He has worked on major construction & logistics projects, with experience in Project, Estates & Facility Management and Procurement Act compliance.  He is a member of UoS Green Impact, an affiliate CIPS member and achieved 3 prestigious Deans awards in 2024/25 for Sustainability, Employability & Student of the year. description: In this illuminating talk, Saptak Chatterjee invites us to rethink the invisible boxes that shape our identities. He explores how success, expectations, and even our greatest strengths can quietly define and limit who we become. Through powerful reflections, he illustrates that true evolution comes not from staying within a single identity, but from having the courage to explore new possibilities while staying rooted in one's authentic self.  Saptak Chatterjee is a singer-songwriter and music producer who creates music from lived emotion rather than spectacle. Trained in Hindustani classical music and audio engineering, he blends tradition with modern sound to tell honest, personal stories. His work speaks to vulnerability, curiosity, and quiet resilience—showing how music can become a space not just entertainment and expression but also for reflection, healing, and genuine human connection. description:
In a world driven by constant notifications, endless opinions, and the relentless pressure to keep up, have we forgotten how to simply be with ourselves?

Tarun Katial explores why silence and self-awareness have become some of the rarest and most valuable assets in today's hyperconnected world. Drawing from his journey across leadership, entrepreneurship, and personal transformation, he challenges the culture of perpetual hustle, comparison, and digital dependency that shapes modern life. He invites the audience to rethink our relationship with technology, expectations, and the constant noise surrounding us and learn how to embrace silence. Tarun Katial has been at the forefront of India's digital revolution for over two decades. As Founder and CEO of Big FM, he built one of India's most beloved radio networks. As CEO of ZEE5, he scaled the platform to over 61 million users and brought iconic shows like Indian Idol and Kaun Banega Crorepati to Indian screens. Now, as Founder and CEO
title: The Power of Silence in a Noisy World  | Tarun Katial | TEDxIIMUdaipur

description:
What we call behavior problems are receipts: evidence of a transaction the system ran long before anyone opened a file. This talk on trauma-informed care and systems change reframes how practitioners, educators, and organizational leaders understand behavior, respond to crisis, and redesign broken institutions.

In our systems, there is a ritual to the way we fail. A moment happens. A meaning gets assigned. A permanent record is created. And repeat.

This talk is for every practitioner, educator, clinical leader, and organizational decision-maker who has watched the files get thicker, and the understanding get thinner, and wondered why every intervention leaves the system exactly where it started.
